period.label: Debut album / Triana cante × Dorantes piano (2001)

works.title: En el compás de su sangre

position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: cante jondo (soleá, seguiriya, tangos) × Triana-Sevilla flamenco lineage with classical/jazz cross-pollination
position_in_era.geographic_locus: Triana, Seville (with family roots in Lebrija through her mother Pepa Vargas)
position_in_era.historical_role: Deep-cante female voice from the Triana-Sevilla axis closest to Dorantes' own family circuit. Daughter of cantaor Curro Fernández and Lebrija-born cantaora Pepa Vargas; her debut album *Esperanza Fernández* (2001, BMG) features Dorantes accompanying her on the canonical soleá *En el compás de su sangre* (lyrics by José de la Tomasa) and on the Romani anthem *Gelem, Gelem*. Dorantes' father and her mother are second cousins — the collaboration is family. She debuted at sixteen with Mario Maya's *Amargo*, then shared stages with Paco de Lucía, Camarón, Enrique Morente and Rafael Riqueni; received the Giraldillo del Cante at the XV Bienal de Flamenco de Sevilla (2008).

narrative_slots.production_facts: Self-titled debut released 17 September 2001 on BMG Music Spain (10 tracks, ~45 min). Dorantes appears on piano on at least *En el compás de su sangre* and *Gelem, Gelem*; also features Garrotín with lyrics by José Saramago. Latin Grammy nomination on debut.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Daughter of Curro Fernández (cantaor) and Pepa Vargas (Lebrija cantaora). Family-tied to Dorantes via her mother (Pepa Vargas) and Dorantes' father being second cousins — same Lebrija-Triana flamenco circuit. Sustained collaborations with Dorantes across decades (the *Recuerdos* project and her broader concert work).
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Triana, Seville — historic Romani flamenco neighbourhood — with the Lebrija family root one generation back. Sits inside the same Sevillian-Romani dynastic web as the Peña-Perrate-Pinini-Bacán family of the Dorantes/Lebrijano line.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Cante (deep soleá / seguiriya register) over flamenco guitar, with Dorantes' piano replacing the guitar on the central tracks. Versatile voice equally at home in flamenco duo, jazz, chamber and symphonic-orchestra contexts.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: *En el compás de su sangre* canonical soleá; the album positioned Esperanza as one of the foremost female cante voices of the 2000s, bridging deep cante and the broader Sevillian art-music circuit.
